subject: Mount St. Helens
title: What If a Volcano Blew Sideways? St. Helens Lost 1,300 Feet in Minutes

scenes.text: What if a volcano exploded sideways? In 1980 one did, and lost its top in minutes.
May 18th, 8:32 a.m. A magnitude 5.1 quake shook Mount St. Helens, and its bulging north face let go.
The largest landslide ever recorded, two thirds of a cubic mile, raced downhill at 150 miles an hour.
That uncorked the volcano. Hot gas and rock shot sideways at over 300 miles an hour and flattened 230 square miles.
In 15 minutes the ash column stood 15 miles high. In three days it crossed the United States. In 15, it circled Earth.
Fifty-seven people died. The summit fell from 9,677 feet to 8,363. The mountain still stands, 1,300 feet shorter, with a hole where the top was.

description:
What if a volcano blew sideways? On 18 May 1980 a magnitude 5.1 quake set off the largest landslide ever recorded on Mount St. Helens, and the lateral blast that followed travelled at over 300 mph and flattened about 230 square miles.
The ash column reached 80,000 feet in 15 minutes, crossed the US in 3 days and circled the globe in 15. The summit fell from 9,677 to 8,363 feet and 57 people died.
What should we run through next?
